content:
The issue is you are using Google or outlook to send your mail and they add it to the sent folder as well as Thunderbird doing it.

You can disable Thunderbird making copies in Account settings. Your mail provider is not considerate enough to allow you to opt out of them doing it, despite it not being something they are supposed to do according to the standard.
creator: MattAuSupport

content:
In your account settings, tell Thunderbird not to place a copy of messages sent into the Sent folder. Presumably the server does this automatically already.

At the top right of the Thunderbird window, click the menu button ≡ > Account Settings > Copies & Folders When sending messages, automatically > uncheck the box 'Place a copy in'

content:
- Assuming you have your old, non-working q.com account is still set up in Thunderbird, you should copy or move any messages you want to keep into Local Folders.

- You should create a brand new account in Thunderbird for your new Yahoo address. Do not try to change the old one to the new one.

- When you're satisfied that the Yahoo account is working properly and you have transferred all the q.com messages to local folders, you can then delete the obsolete q.com account in Thunderbird.

- Be sure to tell all your contacts about your new email address.
